title: The Good Roommate
description: A camera-first chore app for roommates, designed for Apple's foldable iPhone Duo from day one: one layout on the 5.4-inch outer display, a split camera and to-do list on the 7.6-inch inner display.
hmw: make logging a clean room take as little effort as sending a Snap, on a phone that unfolds?

facts.label: My part
facts.value: Everything: product, UX, UI, the iOS app and the backend

facts.label: Platforms
facts.value: iPhone Duo and every iPhone, iOS 27

facts.label: Built on
facts.value: SwiftUI and Liquid Glass, Vision, Supabase

blocks.text: One app, two displays, no seams

iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable: a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner one. I set one rule before any screen: everything works folded and unfolded, and opening or closing the phone mid-task never loses your place.

items.alt: Unfolded iPhone Duo: Up next on the left half, the camera on the right half
items.caption: Unfolded, 7.6 inches: the camera takes the right half and Up next fills the left.

items.alt: Folded iPhone Duo: the camera on the outer display with the tab bar in the side strip
items.caption: Folded, 5.4 inches: the phone layout, with iOS's tab bar moved into the side strip.

blocks.caption: Shown at true relative size, in Apple's iPhone Duo bezels.

items: Folded, the outer display uses the same layout as any iPhone. Unfolded in landscape, the camera takes the right half and the most urgent tasks fill the left.
The split is chosen by display size, not by fold state: it only appears when the screen is wider than tall and its short side is at least 600 points.
The two halves are equal and the camera half is the exact same camera screen as the phone, so there's one camera to design and test, not two.
Fold it mid-task and the app returns to the folded camera with the same task still selected.

items.alt: Unfolded iPhone Duo: the house leaderboard on the left half, the camera on the right half
items.caption: The left half switches between Up next and the leaderboard; the camera stays put.

blocks.text: Folded, iOS moves the status bar and the tab bar into an 84-point strip down the side. I measured it in the simulator as a trailing safe-area inset. A container that ignores the safe area hides it from its children, so the app reads the insets once at the root and keeps everything except the camera feed clear of the strip.
The app opens to the camera

Logging a chore is a photo, so the camera is home. A streak counter sits on it, a pill shows how many tasks are left today, and Up next ranks what's due by what's overdue, what's due soonest, and whose streak is at risk.

items.alt: The camera on iPhone 18 Pro with the streak counter, a Spotted dishwasher chip and the shutter
items.caption: Camera, with on-device detection.

items.alt: The Up next tab on iPhone 18 Pro listing ranked chores with their points
items.caption: Up next, ranked.

blocks.text: Your profile is your streak card, the points you've earned, the chores you've logged, your best streak, your badges and your recent logs. Badges reward the habits the app is for, like a first log, a 7-day streak and 25 chores. A profile is only a display name and an emoji.

items.alt: The Profile page on iPhone 18 Pro: a 12-day streak card, 280 points earned, 28 chores logged, best streak 16, and badges

blocks.text: Anyone can hand a chore to anyone

The House page lists every open chore with who it belongs to. Tap the avatar to hand it to a roommate or back to the whole house, or add a new chore with its room, assignee and due date. The server checks that the assignee lives in the house, and a chore assigned to someone else can only be logged by them.

items.alt: The House page on iPhone 18 Pro listing roommates and open tasks with an assignee on each
items.caption: Every chore shows who has it.

items.alt: The assign menu open over the House tasks: Anyone, You, Maya, Jordan, Sam
items.caption: Reassign in one tap.

items.alt: The New task sheet on iPhone 18 Pro with title, kind, room and who it's assigned to
items.caption: Add a chore and give it to someone.

blocks.text: A leaderboard, and something to spend on

Every chore is worth points. The leaderboard ranks the house this week or all time, and Rewards turns points into perks the house agrees on, like the aux cord, first shower or skipping a chore. Your balance is what you've earned minus what you've spent, and the server checks it and locks it while you redeem, so two quick taps can't spend the same points twice.

items.alt: The Leaderboard tab on iPhone 18 Pro ranking the four roommates by points this week
items.caption: The house, ranked.

items.alt: The Rewards page on iPhone 18 Pro with a 220-point balance and the house rewards with their costs
items.caption: Points to spend.

items.alt: Redeeming a reward: an Aux cord is yours confirmation over the Rewards page
items.caption: Redeemed.

blocks.text: A tiny story before the points

Logging the trash plays a short SF Symbols story: the can drops in, the lid swings open, a bag falls in, the lid slams shut, stars burst, then +10. Every chore has its own beat with a haptic on each, the points land at 1.7 seconds, and the whole thing stays under 3 seconds. Reduce Motion skips straight to the points.

image.alt: Animated sequence: a trash can opens, a bag drops in, the lid shuts and stars burst before the points appear

blocks.caption: The trash story, captured from the app.

blocks.text: The camera knows what you're pointing at

Apple's Vision classifier runs on the phone about twice a second. The app maps what it sees to rooms and chores, smooths the guess over five frames, and only then shows a chip like "Spotted dishwasher · Dishes +20". It pauses when the camera tab is hidden, the phone is hot, or Low Power Mode is on. No frame is stored or sent; at most three labels are saved with a log.
A name, an emoji, and nothing else

items: A profile is a display name and an emoji. Email stays with the sign-in provider, and there are no tracking identifiers or analytics.
Chore photos lose their location and camera data on the phone, live in a private bucket only the house can read, and are deleted after 7 days.
The server sets the time and the points on every log, so a phone can't backdate a chore or award itself points.
Invite codes rotate every 24 hours and can be shared as a QR code, through the share sheet, or by holding two phones together.

items.alt: The House page on iPhone 18 Pro with a QR code invite, the code, a countdown to the next code, and Share invite and Hold phones together buttons
items.caption: A rotating QR invite.

blocks.text: The iOS 27 app is SwiftUI with tinted Liquid Glass. The rules (streaks, ranking, points, invite codes, matching camera labels to chores) live in a plain Swift package with 53 tests, so the same logic can reach Android through Skip later. Supabase handles sign-in with Apple, Google or an emailed code, the data with row-level security on every table, and live updates between roommates.

I ran it like a product team: a decision log, an ideas backlog with statuses, versioned screenshots for every release, and a Linear project. I built it with Claude Code leading and reviewing, and Google's Antigravity and smaller models taking scoped tickets. The screenshots on this page come from UI tests that drive the app and frame each screen in Apple's bezels.
